sections.title: Nic Colarossi
sections.sub: I run continuous monitoring for SAP Concur’s FedRAMP environment — vulnerabilities, evidence, change review, and the report that has to land on time.

sections.title: What I do
sections.lede: Day-to-day security operations on a small team for an authorized SaaS platform. The work is tracking, hunting, writing controls, and automating the parts that used to eat a week.

items.heading: Continuous monitoring, automated
items.body: Python, PowerShell, Bash, and Power Automate now produce the POA&M and ConMon evidence that used to be a week of copy-paste. Same package. Less theater.

items.heading: Hunting that becomes a finding
items.body: Splunk, Kibana, Nessus, and SQL extracts from Concur. If it matters, it goes on the risk register or the POA&M — not a slide that dies in a meeting.

items.heading: CR2026 / 20x ops app
items.body: Internal SAP CAP + UI5 app used by the ConMon team for VDR, VER, SCN, and SDR workflows and KSI connectors. Built with Claude Code. OSCAL POA&M export is next.

items.heading: AI features inside an authorization
items.body: Advise on data handling, significant-change review, and monitoring before AI capabilities reach the FedRAMP-authorized production path.

sections.title: Experience
sections.lede: SAP America, Newtown Square. Three roles, same company.

bullets: Vulnerability tracking, evidence collection, change review, ISSO communication, agency reporting.
Prioritize ~300 open POA&M items with system owners.
Wrote SSP language accepted for SC-13, AU-2, and related SC / AU controls.
Completed IL-5 and CMMC gap analyses.
SAML, OAuth, PKI, and TLS/SSL failures — diagnose, then walk the customer and engineering through the fix.
SQL investigations and KBAs that cut repeat identity and certificate tickets.

items.when: Mar 2021 — Mar 2022 · contract, US Experts Team
bullets: Escalated access and technical incidents for about 100,000 internal users (ServiceNow, Azure AD / SCCM, Jamf).
